source.text: Ἐν δὲ ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις παραγίνεται Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστὴς κηρύσσων ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ λέγων· Μετανοεῖτε, ἤγγικεν γὰρ ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.

records.literal_gloss: In then the days those comes John the Baptist preaching in the wilderness of the Judea \v 2 and saying, Repent, has come near for the kingdom of the heavens.

en.L: In those days John the Baptist comes, preaching in the wilderness of Judea \v 2 and saying, "Repent, for the kingdom of the heavens has come near."
en.B: In those days John the Baptist appeared in the wilderness of Judea with a message. \v 2 "Repent," he proclaimed, "because the kingdom of heaven has come near."
en.R: At that time John the Baptist came to the desert land of Judea and preached to the people. \v 2 He said, "Turn away from your sins and come back to God, because the kingdom of heaven is coming near."

fr.L: Or en ces jours-là paraît Jean le Baptiste, proclamant dans le désert de Judée \v 2 et disant : « Repentez-vous, car le royaume des cieux s’est approché. »
fr.B: En ces jours-là, Jean le Baptiste parut dans le désert de Judée avec un message. \v 2 « Repentez-vous, proclamait-il, car le royaume des cieux s’est approché. »
fr.R: À cette époque, Jean le Baptiste est venu dans le désert de Judée, et il s’est mis à parler aux gens. \v 2 Il disait : « Détournez-vous de vos péchés et revenez à Dieu, car le royaume des cieux est tout proche. »

decisions.choice: in those days: a loose link, years after chapter 2
alternatives: the same time as the move to Nazareth
decisions.reason: The phrase is a common way to open a new part of the story. Jesus is now a grown man (3:13).

decisions.choice: repent: change one's mind and way of life, turning back to God
decisions.reason: The word means a change of mind. In the prophets' call to Israel to return to God, it is a turning of the whole life, which John asks to see in deeds (3:8).

decisions.choice: the kingdom of heaven: God's rule, the kingdom of God
alternatives: a place in heaven where people go after death
decisions.reason: Matthew nearly always says "kingdom of heaven" where Mark and Luke say "kingdom of God" (compare 4:17 with Mark 1:15), as Jews often spoke of heaven out of reverence for God's name. It is God's reign coming to earth, as in the prayer "your kingdom come" (6:10).

decisions.choice: has come near: it is close at hand, already pressing in
decisions.reason: The perfect tense says the kingdom has drawn near and is now close. Jesus will announce it in the same words (4:17).

decisions.choice: the kingdom of heaven (B, R); the kingdom of the heavens (L)
decisions.reason: "Heavens" is plural in Greek, following Hebrew. Balanced and Readable say "heaven", as English does, and keep Matthew's phrase, which the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: turn away from your sins and come back to God; the desert land
decisions.reason: Readable says what repenting means, and calls the wilderness by a word new readers know. It was dry, empty country, not sand desert.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); historic presents kept as presents at Literal ("paraît", "arrive", "laisse")
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 1-2 and the other Gospels: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken. Speech keeps its own tenses at every level. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: le royaume des cieux at every level (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet. English Balanced and Readable say "heaven", but French keeps the plural "des cieux", which is the set phrase in French and is not hard for new readers; the meaning note says it is God's rule (m3). "Royaume" as in Mark's and Luke's "royaume de Dieu".

decisions.choice: repentez-vous, la repentance (L, B); détournez-vous de vos péchés et revenez à Dieu (R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet and Mark: Readable says what repenting means (m2), as the English does.

source.text: οὗτος γάρ ἐστιν ὁ ῥηθεὶς διὰ Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· Φωνὴ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ· Ἑτοιμάσατε τὴν ὁδὸν κυρίου, εὐθείας ποιεῖτε τὰς τρίβους αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: This for is the [one] spoken through Isaiah the prophet saying, Voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of Lord, straight make the paths of him.

en.L: For this is the one spoken of through Isaiah the prophet, saying, "[The] voice of one crying out in the wilderness: 'Prepare the way of [the] Lord, make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} paths straight.'"
en.B: John is the one the prophet Isaiah spoke of when he said, "A voice is calling out in the wilderness: 'Prepare the way of the Lord, straighten the roads {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will travel.'"
en.R: The prophet Isaiah spoke about John when he said, "Someone is shouting in the desert: 'Get the road ready for the Lord! Make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} paths straight!'"

fr.L: Car c’est lui dont il a été parlé par l’intermédiaire d’Ésaïe le prophète, disant : « Voix de quelqu’un qui crie dans le désert : “Préparez le chemin du Seigneur, rendez droits {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} sentiers.” »
fr.B: C’est de Jean qu’avait parlé le prophète Ésaïe, quand il disait : « Une voix crie dans le désert : “Préparez le chemin du Seigneur, aplanissez les routes où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} passera.” »
fr.R: Le prophète Ésaïe parlait de Jean quand il a dit : « Quelqu’un crie dans le désert : “Préparez la route pour le Seigneur ! Rendez {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} chemins bien droits !” »

decisions.choice: Isaiah 40:3: the voice that prepares the Lord's road home
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 40 a voice calls for a road to be made ready for God, who is coming to bring his people back from exile. Matthew quotes the Greek Old Testament, which joins "in the wilderness" to the voice; the Hebrew joins it to "prepare". Either way John fits: he preaches in the wilderness.

decisions.choice: the Lord: God in Isaiah; the one John prepares for is Jesus
alternatives: God alone, with no thought of Jesus
decisions.reason: In Isaiah the Lord is God, whose name stands in the Hebrew. John prepares the way for the one coming after him (3:11), who is Jesus (3:13-17). Matthew lets the words for God's coming describe Jesus's coming.

decisions.choice: this is the one: Matthew's comment, not John's
decisions.reason: "For" introduces the narrator's explanation of who John is.

decisions.choice: his paths (L, R); the roads he will travel (B), with deity_pronoun spans
alternatives: no span, as for a pronoun for God in Isaiah
decisions.reason: The pronoun is for the Lord, whom Matthew identifies with Jesus, so it takes the usual span.

decisions.choice: John (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name John for clarity.

source.text: αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ Ἰωάννης εἶχεν τὸ ἔνδυμα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τριχῶν καμήλου καὶ ζώνην δερματίνην περὶ τὴν ὀσφὺν αὐτοῦ, ἡ δὲ τροφὴ ἦν αὐτοῦ ἀκρίδες καὶ μέλι ἄγριον.

records.literal_gloss: He then the John had the garment of him from hairs of camel and a belt leathern around the waist of him, the then food was of him locusts and honey wild.

en.L: Now John himself had his clothing of camel's hair and a leather belt around his waist, and his food was locusts and wild honey.
en.B: John himself dressed in clothing woven from camel's hair, with a leather belt around his waist, and he ate locusts and wild honey.
en.R: John wore clothes made from camel hair, with a leather belt around his waist. He ate locusts, a kind of grasshopper, and honey that he found in the wild.

fr.L: Or Jean lui-même avait son vêtement de poils de chameau et une ceinture de cuir autour de ses reins, et sa nourriture était des sauterelles et du miel sauvage.
fr.B: Jean portait un vêtement tissé de poils de chameau, avec une ceinture de cuir autour de la taille, et il se nourrissait de sauterelles et de miel sauvage.
fr.R: Jean portait des vêtements faits en poils de chameau, avec une ceinture de cuir autour de la taille. Il mangeait des sauterelles et du miel qu’il trouvait dans la nature.

decisions.choice: camel's hair and a leather belt: the dress of Elijah
decisions.reason: Elijah was known as a hairy man with a leather belt around his waist (2 Kings 1:8). Malachi promised that Elijah would come before the day of the Lord (Malachi 4:5), and Jesus later says that John is the Elijah who was to come (11:14; 17:12-13).

decisions.choice: locusts and wild honey: food found in the wilderness
decisions.reason: The law allows locusts as food (Leviticus 11:22). Wild honey was taken from wild bees. John lives on what the wilderness provides, apart from towns.

decisions.choice: locusts, a kind of grasshopper
decisions.reason: Readable says what locusts are.

decisions.choice: des sauterelles, with no explanation at Readable
decisions.reason: As in Mark 1:6: English Readable explains "locusts" as a kind of grasshopper. French "sauterelle" is already the everyday name of that insect, so Readable needs no gloss.

source.text: τότε ἐξεπορεύετο πρὸς αὐτὸν Ἱεροσόλυμα καὶ πᾶσα ἡ Ἰουδαία καὶ πᾶσα ἡ περίχωρος τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, καὶ ἐβαπτίζοντο ἐν τῷ Ἰορδάνῃ ποταμῷ ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ ἐξομολογούμενοι τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Then were going out to him Jerusalem and all the Judea and all the region around the Jordan, \v 6 and were being baptized in the Jordan river by him confessing the sins of them.

en.L: Then Jerusalem and all Judea and all the region around the Jordan were going out to him, \v 6 and they were being baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
en.B: Crowds kept coming out to him from Jerusalem, from all over Judea, and from all the country along the Jordan. \v 6 They confessed their sins, and he baptized them in the Jordan River.
en.R: People from Jerusalem, from all over Judea, and from all the land near the Jordan River came out to John. \v 6 They told how they had done wrong, and John baptized them in the Jordan River.

fr.L: Alors sortaient vers lui Jérusalem, et toute la Judée, et toute la région autour du Jourdain, \v 6 et ils étaient baptisés par lui dans le fleuve Jourdain, confessant leurs péchés.
fr.B: Des foules venaient à lui sans cesse, de Jérusalem, de toute la Judée et de toute la région qui borde le Jourdain. \v 6 Elles confessaient leurs péchés, et il les baptisait dans le Jourdain.
fr.R: Des gens venaient voir Jean : ils venaient de Jérusalem, de toute la Judée et de toute la région près du fleuve Jourdain. \v 6 Ils disaient le mal qu’ils avaient fait, et Jean les baptisait dans le fleuve Jourdain.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem and all Judea: the people of those places, in great numbers
decisions.reason: The places stand for their people, and "all" stresses how many came. The imperfect verbs say they kept coming.

decisions.choice: baptized: dipped or washed in water
decisions.reason: The verb means to dip or immerse. Jews washed in water to become clean for worship. John's washing, given once and joined to confessing sins, marked a turning back to God ahead of the coming judgment.

decisions.choice: confessing their sins: saying openly what they had done wrong
alternatives: admitting sin only in their hearts
decisions.reason: The verb means to acknowledge out loud. They named their sins as they came to be baptized.

decisions.choice: crowds kept coming (B); people ... came (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people instead of the places.

source.text: Ἰδὼν δὲ πολλοὺς τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων ἐρχομένους ἐπὶ τὸ βάπτισμα αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν, τίς ὑπέδειξεν ὑμῖν φυγεῖν ἀπὸ τῆς μελλούσης ὀργῆς;

records.literal_gloss: Having seen then many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to the baptism of him he said to them, Offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?

en.L: But seeing many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, he said to them, "Offspring of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?
en.B: But when John saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming for baptism, he said to them, "You family of snakes! Who warned you to run from the coming wrath?
en.R: Many Pharisees and Sadducees also came to be baptized. When John saw them, he said to them, "You are like a family of poisonous snakes! Who told you that you could escape from God's anger that is coming?

fr.L: Mais voyant beaucoup de Pharisiens et de Sadducéens venir à son baptême, il leur dit : « Progéniture de vipères ! Qui vous a avertis de fuir la colère à venir ?
fr.B: Mais quand Jean vit beaucoup de Pharisiens et de Sadducéens venir se faire baptiser, il leur dit : « Nichée de vipères ! Qui vous a avertis de fuir la colère qui vient ?
fr.R: Beaucoup de Pharisiens et de Sadducéens sont venus, eux aussi, pour se faire baptiser. Quand Jean les a vus, il leur a dit : « Vous êtes comme une famille de serpents venimeux ! Qui vous a dit que vous pourriez échapper à la colère de Dieu qui va venir ?

decisions.choice: Pharisees and Sadducees: two leading groups among the Jews
decisions.reason: The Pharisees were teachers and lay people devoted to keeping the law in detail. The Sadducees were mostly priests and wealthy families tied to the temple. The two groups often disagreed; Matthew names them together as Israel's leaders (16:1, 6).

decisions.choice: coming to his baptism: coming to be baptized
alternatives: coming to watch where he baptized
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean coming for baptism or coming to the place of baptism. John's answer, which questions why they would flee and asks for fruit, fits people who came to be baptized.

decisions.choice: offspring of vipers: people as dangerous and false as poisonous snakes
decisions.reason: Calling people children of something describes their nature. Jesus uses the same words for the Pharisees (12:34; 23:33).

decisions.choice: the coming wrath: God's judgment that is about to fall
decisions.reason: Wrath here is God's anger against sin at the judgment (1 Thessalonians 1:10). John sees it as near (3:10, 12).

decisions.choice: John
decisions.reason: A new paragraph begins here, so Balanced names John.

decisions.choice: you family of snakes (B); you are like a family of poisonous snakes (R)
decisions.reason: "Brood" and "viper" are less common words today. Readable makes the comparison plain.

decisions.choice: God's anger
decisions.reason: Readable says whose anger it is.

decisions.choice: les Pharisiens, les Sadducéens, capitalised (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet, John, Mark and Luke: the names of the groups take a capital, as in English.

decisions.choice: Progéniture de vipères (L); Nichée de vipères (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek "offspring". "Race de vipères" is the traditional wording, but "race" now sounds like ethnicity; Balanced says "nichée", a brood of young snakes, which keeps the insult of the family picture (m3).

source.text: ποιήσατε οὖν καρπὸν ἄξιον τῆς μετανοίας καὶ μὴ δόξητε λέγειν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· Πατέρα ἔχομεν τὸν Ἀβραάμ, λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι δύναται ὁ θεὸς ἐκ τῶν λίθων τούτων ἐγεῖραι τέκνα τῷ Ἀβραάμ.

records.literal_gloss: Produce therefore fruit worthy of the repentance \v 9 and not think to say among yourselves, [As] father we have the Abraham, I say for to you that is able the God out of the stones these to raise up children to the Abraham.

en.L: Produce therefore fruit worthy of repentance, \v 9 and do not presume to say among yourselves, 'We have Abraham [as] father,' for I tell you that God is able from these stones to raise up children for Abraham.
en.B: So produce fruit that shows your repentance is real. \v 9 Do not imagine you can comfort yourselves by saying, 'Abraham is our father.' I tell you, God is able to make children for Abraham out of these stones.
en.R: Show by the way you live that you have really turned away from your sins. \v 9 Do not think, 'We are safe, because Abraham is our ancestor.' I tell you, God could make children for Abraham out of these stones.

fr.L: Produisez donc du fruit digne de la repentance, \v 9 et ne pensez pas pouvoir dire en vous-mêmes : “Nous avons Abraham [pour] père”, car je vous dis que Dieu peut, de ces pierres, susciter des enfants à Abraham.
fr.B: Produisez donc un fruit qui montre que votre repentance est sincère. \v 9 Et n’allez pas vous rassurer en vous disant : “Abraham est notre père.” Car je vous le dis, de ces pierres que voici, Dieu peut faire naître des enfants à Abraham.
fr.R: Montrez par votre façon de vivre que vous vous êtes vraiment détournés de vos péchés. \v 9 Ne pensez pas : “Nous ne risquons rien, parce qu’Abraham est notre ancêtre.” Je vous le dis, Dieu pourrait faire de ces pierres des enfants pour Abraham.

decisions.choice: fruit worthy of repentance: deeds that match a changed life
decisions.reason: Fruit is a picture of what a life produces. John asks for a changed life to show itself in deeds (7:16-20).

decisions.choice: We have Abraham as father: trust that belonging to Abraham's family is enough
decisions.reason: God's promises to Abraham and his descendants (Genesis 17:7) could be taken as a guarantee for every descendant. John says descent does not take the place of repentance.

decisions.choice: from these stones children: perhaps a play on words
decisions.reason: In Hebrew and Aramaic the words for "stones" and "sons" sound alike. If John spoke Aramaic, his hearers may have heard the play. Isaiah 51:1-2 also calls Abraham the rock from which Israel was cut.

decisions.choice: fruit that shows your repentance is real (B); show by the way you live (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture and says what it shows; Readable states the meaning.

decisions.choice: We are safe, because Abraham is our ancestor
alternatives: We have Abraham as our father
decisions.reason: Readable states what the saying was meant to claim.

source.text: ἤδη δὲ ἡ ἀξίνη πρὸς τὴν ῥίζαν τῶν δένδρων κεῖται· πᾶν οὖν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλὸν ἐκκόπτεται καὶ εἰς πῦρ βάλλεται.

records.literal_gloss: Already then the ax at the root of the trees lies; every therefore tree not producing fruit good is cut down and into fire is thrown.

en.L: And already the ax lies at the root of the trees; so every tree not producing good fruit is cut down and thrown into [the] fire.
en.B: The ax is already set against the root of the trees. Any tree that fails to bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
en.R: The ax is ready at the roots of the trees. God's judgment is that close. Every tree that does not grow good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.

fr.L: Et déjà la hache est placée à la racine des arbres ; tout arbre donc qui ne produit pas de bon fruit est coupé et jeté au feu.
fr.B: La hache est déjà posée contre la racine des arbres. Tout arbre qui ne porte pas de bon fruit, on l’abat et on le jette au feu.
fr.R: La hache est prête, au pied des arbres. Le jugement de Dieu est aussi proche que cela. Tout arbre qui ne donne pas de bons fruits sera coupé et jeté dans le feu.

decisions.choice: the ax at the root: judgment is about to fall
decisions.reason: The ax is laid at the root, ready for the first stroke. The trees are the people; the fire is God's judgment (3:12; 7:19).

decisions.choice: is cut down, is thrown: certain, and as good as happening
alternatives: a general rule with no reference to time
decisions.reason: The present tense speaks of what will surely happen as if it were already under way.

decisions.choice: God's judgment is that close
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture and says what it means.

source.text: Ἐγὼ μὲν ὑμᾶς βαπτίζω ἐν ὕδατι εἰς μετάνοιαν· ὁ δὲ ὀπίσω μου ἐρχόμενος ἰσχυρότερός μού ἐστιν, οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς τὰ ὑποδήματα βαστάσαι· αὐτὸς ὑμᾶς βαπτίσει ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ καὶ πυρί·

records.literal_gloss: I indeed you baptize in water for repentance; the but after me coming stronger than me is, of whom not I am fit the sandals to carry; he you will baptize in Spirit Holy and fire;

en.L: I baptize you in water for repentance, but the one coming after me is stronger than I, whose sandals I am not fit to carry; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will baptize you in [the] Holy Spirit and fire.
en.B: I baptize you with water for repentance. But one who comes after me is mightier than I am, and I am not fit even to carry {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.
en.R: I baptize you with water to show that you have turned away from your sins. But someone is coming after me who is much greater than I am. I am not good enough even to carry {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.

fr.L: Moi, je vous baptise dans l’eau en vue de la repentance ; mais celui qui vient après moi est plus fort que moi, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dont je ne suis pas apte à porter les sandales ; {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} vous baptisera dans l’Esprit Saint et le feu.
fr.B: Moi, je vous baptise avec de l’eau, en vue de la repentance. Mais celui qui vient après moi est plus puissant que moi, et je ne suis même pas digne de porter {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} sandales. Lui vous baptisera avec l’Esprit Saint et avec le feu.
fr.R: Moi, je vous baptise avec de l’eau pour montrer que vous vous êtes détournés de vos péchés. Mais quelqu’un vient après moi, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est beaucoup plus grand que moi. Je ne suis même pas assez bon pour porter {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} sandales. Lui vous baptisera avec l’Esprit Saint et avec le feu.

decisions.choice: for repentance: a baptism that goes with turning back to God
alternatives: a baptism that brings about repentance
a baptism because they had repented
decisions.reason: The phrase says only that John's baptism has to do with repentance. It may call people to repent or mark their repenting; John's demand for fruit (3:8) suggests both.

decisions.choice: the one coming after me: the Messiah, whom John does not name
decisions.reason: John speaks of someone greater who will come after him. The next scene shows that it is Jesus (3:13-17).

decisions.choice: carry his sandals: the task of the lowest slave
decisions.reason: Carrying or untying a master's sandals was a slave's job. John says he is not worthy even of that.

decisions.choice: with the Holy Spirit and fire: the Spirit for those who repent, fire as judgment
alternatives: the Spirit and fire as one cleansing gift
fire as the Spirit's power only
decisions.reason: "You" has one verb and one preposition for both, so the baptism is one act. In the verses before and after, fire is judgment (3:10, 12), and the wheat and the chaff are two groups. Others read the fire as the Spirit's cleansing (Malachi 3:2-3).

decisions.choice: in water, in the Holy Spirit (L); with water, with the Holy Spirit (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek preposition can mean "in" or "with". Literal keeps "in", the picture of being immersed; Balanced and Readable use the usual English "with".

decisions.choice: to show that you have turned away from your sins
decisions.reason: Readable gives one of the senses the meaning note describes; the note says the phrase may also be a call to repent.

decisions.choice: apte (L); digne (B)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 1:7: the word means fit for a task. Literal keeps that sense with "apte"; "je ne suis pas digne de" is the natural French way to say one is not fit even for the lowest service (m3).

source.text: οὗ τὸ πτύον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ διακαθαριεῖ τὴν ἅλωνα αὐτοῦ καὶ συνάξει τὸν σῖτον αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν ἀποθήκην, τὸ δὲ ἄχυρον κατακαύσει πυρὶ ἀσβέστῳ.

records.literal_gloss: Of whom the winnowing fork in the hand of him, and he will clear out the threshing floor of him and will gather the wheat of him into the barn, the but chaff he will burn up with fire unquenchable.

en.L: His winnowing fork [is] in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will clear out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} threshing floor and gather {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wheat into the barn, but the chaff {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will burn up with unquenchable fire."
en.B: He has {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} winnowing fork in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will clear {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} threshing floor. He will gather {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wheat into the barn, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will burn up the chaff with a fire that cannot be put out."
en.R: He is like a farmer who is ready to separate wheat from chaff. He has the tool for it in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand. He will clean {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} threshing floor and put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wheat in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} barn. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will burn the chaff in a fire that never goes out."

fr.L: Sa pelle à vanner [est] dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nettoiera {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} aire, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} rassemblera {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} blé dans le grenier, mais la balle, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} la brûlera dans un feu inextinguible. »
fr.B: Il tient en {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} pelle à vanner, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} va nettoyer {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} aire. Il amassera {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} blé dans le grenier, mais la paille, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} la brûlera dans un feu qui ne s’éteint jamais. »
fr.R: Il est comme un paysan prêt à séparer le grain de la paille. Il a l’outil pour le faire dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main. Il va nettoyer l’endroit où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} bat le blé, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} va mettre {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} blé dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} grenier. Mais la paille, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} la brûlera dans un feu qui ne s’éteint jamais. »

decisions.choice: winnowing fork, threshing floor, chaff: the work of separating grain at harvest
decisions.reason: After threshing, a farmer tossed the grain into the wind with a wooden fork on a hard, open floor. The wind carried off the light chaff and the grain fell back. The grain was stored, and the chaff was burned.

decisions.choice: the one coming will separate people at the judgment
alternatives: a picture of everyday life only
decisions.reason: The wheat and the chaff are the people who repent and those who do not, as with the good and bad trees of 3:10. Jesus uses the same kind of picture in 13:30.

decisions.choice: unquenchable fire: fire that no one can put out
alternatives: fire that burns for a short time
decisions.reason: The fire of judgment cannot be stopped (Isaiah 66:24; Mark 9:43, 48).

decisions.choice: whose: the relative ties this to 3:11, the one who is coming
decisions.reason: The verse begins with "whose", so it goes on speaking of the one coming after John.

decisions.choice: His winnowing fork (L); He has his winnowing fork (B); He is like a farmer (R)
decisions.reason: English does not begin a new sentence with "whose", so the levels begin with "his" or "he". Readable says the farmer is a comparison.

decisions.choice: la balle (L); la paille (B, R)
decisions.reason: "La balle" is the exact French word for the husks blown off the grain, but most readers today know it only as "ball". Balanced and Readable say "la paille", the everyday word for what is left once the grain is taken (m1).

source.text: Τότε παραγίνεται ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰορδάνην πρὸς τὸν Ἰωάννην τοῦ βαπτισθῆναι ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Then comes the Jesus from the Galilee to the Jordan to the John to be baptized by him.

en.L: Then Jesus comes from Galilee to the Jordan, to John, to be baptized by him.
en.B: Then Jesus arrived from Galilee and came to John at the Jordan, to be baptized by him.
en.R: Then Jesus traveled from Galilee to the Jordan River. He came to John so that John would baptize {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

fr.L: Alors Jésus arrive de Galilée au Jourdain, auprès de Jean, pour être baptisé par lui.
fr.B: Alors Jésus vint de Galilée au Jourdain, auprès de Jean, pour se faire baptiser par lui.
fr.R: Ensuite, Jésus est venu de Galilée jusqu’au fleuve Jourdain. Il est allé voir Jean pour que Jean {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} baptise.

decisions.choice: to be baptized: Jesus comes for this purpose
decisions.reason: The verb form states his purpose. Jesus seeks baptism; John's protest follows.

decisions.choice: comes (L); came, arrived (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration; Balanced and Readable use the past.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰωάννης διεκώλυεν αὐτὸν λέγων· Ἐγὼ χρείαν ἔχω ὑπὸ σοῦ βαπτισθῆναι, καὶ σὺ ἔρχῃ πρός με;

records.literal_gloss: The but John was preventing him saying, I need by you to be baptized, and you come to me?

en.L: But John tried to prevent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "I need to be baptized by {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come to me?"
en.B: John tried to stop {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. "I am the one who needs to be baptized by {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}," he said, "and yet {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come to me?"
en.R: But John tried to talk {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out of it. He said, "I should be baptized by {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}! Why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} coming to me?"

fr.L: Mais Jean cherchait à {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}en empêcher, disant : « Moi, j’ai besoin d’être baptisé par {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, et {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} viens à moi ? »
fr.B: Jean tenta de {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}en dissuader : « C’est moi qui ai besoin d’être baptisé par {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, dit-il, et c’est {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui viens à moi ? »
fr.R: Mais Jean a essayé de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} faire changer d’avis. Il {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a dit : « C’est moi qui devrais être baptisé par {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ! Pourquoi est-ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} viens vers moi ? »

decisions.choice: tried to prevent: he kept trying to stop him
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense describes an attempt, which Jesus overcomes (3:15).

decisions.choice: I ... you: John sets himself below Jesus
decisions.reason: Both pronouns are written out for emphasis. John has said he is not fit to carry the sandals of the one who comes (3:11).

source.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἄφες ἄρτι, οὕτως γὰρ πρέπον ἐστὶν ἡμῖν πληρῶσαι πᾶσαν δικαιοσύνην.

records.literal_gloss: Answering then the Jesus said to him, Permit now, thus for fitting it is to us to fulfill all righteousness.

en.L: But answering, Jesus said to him, "Permit [it] now, for in this way it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness."
en.B: But Jesus answered, "Allow it for now. This is the fitting way for us to fulfill all righteousness."
en.R: Jesus answered, "Let it happen this way for now. We should do everything that is righteous in God's eyes, and this is part of it."

fr.L: Mais répondant, Jésus lui dit : « Laisse [faire] maintenant, car c’est ainsi qu’il nous convient d’accomplir toute justice. »
fr.B: Mais Jésus lui répondit : « Accepte pour l’instant. C’est ainsi qu’il convient que nous accomplissions toute justice. »
fr.R: Jésus lui a répondu : « Laisse faire pour le moment. Nous devons faire tout ce qui est juste aux yeux de Dieu, et cela en fait partie. »

decisions.choice: fulfill all righteousness: do all that God wills and requires
alternatives: carry out God's plan to save his people
keep every rule of the law
decisions.reason: In Matthew righteousness is doing God's will (5:6, 10, 20; 6:33). Jesus, though greater than John, takes his place with the people who come in obedience to God's call. Some see a wider sense: completing God's saving purpose.

decisions.choice: us: Jesus and John together
decisions.reason: Both have a part: John in baptizing and Jesus in being baptized.

decisions.choice: now: for the present
decisions.reason: The word says the order John expected is set aside for the time being.

decisions.choice: do everything that is righteous in God's eyes
decisions.reason: "Fulfill righteousness" is not plain English. Readable keeps the key word and says whose standard is meant.

fr.B: Alors Jean {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} laissa se faire baptiser.
fr.R: Alors Jean a accepté de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} baptiser.

decisions.choice: permits him: allows him to be baptized
decisions.reason: The verb is the one Jesus used: "permit it". John gives way.

decisions.choice: let him be baptized (B); agreed to baptize him (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what John permitted.

source.text: βαπτισθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εὐθὺς ἀνέβη ἀπὸ τοῦ ὕδατος· καὶ ἰδοὺ ἠνεῴχθησαν οἱ οὐρανοί, καὶ εἶδεν πνεῦμα θεοῦ καταβαῖνον ὡσεὶ περιστερὰν ἐρχόμενον ἐπ’ αὐτόν·

records.literal_gloss: Having been baptized then the Jesus immediately went up from the water; and behold, were opened the heavens, and he saw Spirit of God descending as a dove coming upon him;

en.L: And when Jesus had been baptized, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} immediately went up from the water, and look, the heavens were opened, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw [the] Spirit of God descending like a dove, coming upon {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Jesus was baptized, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came straight up out of the water. Suddenly the heavens opened, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw the Spirit of God coming down like a dove and settling on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: After Jesus was baptized, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came up out of the water right away. Then heaven opened, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw the Spirit of God coming down on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} like a dove.

fr.L: Et ayant été baptisé, Jésus remonta aussitôt de l’eau ; et voici, les cieux furent ouverts, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vit l’Esprit de Dieu descendre comme une colombe, venant sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Dès qu’il eut été baptisé, Jésus sortit de l’eau. Soudain les cieux s’ouvrirent, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vit l’Esprit de Dieu descendre comme une colombe et se poser sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Après avoir été baptisé, Jésus est tout de suite sorti de l’eau. Alors le ciel s’est ouvert, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a vu l’Esprit de Dieu descendre sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} comme une colombe.

decisions.choice: the heavens were opened: God shows himself and speaks
decisions.reason: When heaven opens in Scripture, God is giving a vision or coming to help (Ezekiel 1:1; Isaiah 64:1).

decisions.choice: like a dove: the Spirit's coming is compared to a dove
alternatives: the Spirit took the bodily form of a dove (Luke 3:22)
decisions.reason: Matthew says only that the Spirit came down like a dove; it may describe the Spirit's form or the way it came down. Luke says "in bodily form".

decisions.choice: the Spirit upon him: God's Spirit resting on his chosen one
decisions.reason: Isaiah promised that God's Spirit would rest on the branch from Jesse (Isaiah 11:2) and on God's servant (Isaiah 42:1). Matthew quotes the second passage of Jesus in 12:18.

decisions.choice: the heavens were opened, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the heavens were opened to him, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "to him". The SBLGNT leaves it out. Either way Jesus is the one who sees. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: look (L); suddenly (B); then (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: Matthew uses this word to point to what comes next. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal uses "look", and Balanced and Readable carry its force in the flow of the sentence, as in 1:20.

source.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ φωνὴ ἐκ τῶν οὐρανῶν λέγουσα· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν ᾧ εὐδόκησα.

records.literal_gloss: And behold, a voice out of the heavens saying, This is the son of me the beloved, in whom I was well pleased.

en.L: And look, a voice out of the heavens, saying, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son, the beloved, in whom I am well pleased."
en.B: And a voice spoke from heaven: "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dearly loved Son, and I delight in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.R: Then a voice from heaven said, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son, and I love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. I am very pleased with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

fr.L: Et voici, une voix [venant] des cieux, disant : « Celui-ci est {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Fils, le bien-aimé, en qui je prends plaisir. »
fr.B: Et une voix se fit entendre du ciel : « Celui-ci est {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Fils bien-aimé ; en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} je trouve {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} joie. »
fr.R: Puis une voix venant du ciel a dit : « Voici {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Fils, et je {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}aime. Je suis très content de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. »

decisions.choice: my Son ... in whom I am well pleased: Psalm 2:7 and Isaiah 42:1
decisions.reason: In Psalm 2:7 God says to his anointed king, "You are my son." In Isaiah 42:1 God speaks of his servant, "in whom my soul delights", on whom he puts his Spirit (3:16). The voice calls Jesus both the king and the servant. "Beloved" may also recall Abraham's beloved son Isaac (Genesis 22:2).

decisions.choice: I am well pleased: a settled delight
alternatives: I was pleased at one moment in the past
decisions.reason: The past tense expresses God's delight as decided and complete, not limited to one moment.

decisions.choice: This is: the voice speaks about Jesus to those present
decisions.reason: Mark 1:11 and Luke 3:22 have "You are". In Matthew the voice announces who Jesus is, as at the transfiguration (17:5).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: Matthew uses this word to point to what comes next. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal uses "look", and Balanced and Readable carry its force in the flow of the sentence, as in 1:20.

decisions.choice: Son with a capital letter
decisions.reason: When God calls Jesus his Son, the word is a title, written with a capital letter as in John. In 2:15 the quotation from Hosea keeps the lower case, since there it first spoke of Israel.
